content:
alex: FYI a customer hit a weird one — several users got stripped of RBAC roles after a SCIM sync. They see 429s on our SCIM endpoint and intermittent KMS decrypt errors in the audit logs. Can we triage?

maria: Ugh. Which IdP? Okta or AAD? Any reproducible pattern/timestamp?

alex: Okta. Reported window: 2026-03-18 14:20-14:45 UTC. Posting the small snippet they forwarded: 

chris: paste the logs here (redact PII)

alex: ```
2026-03-18T14:21:03Z WARN scim-provisioner request_id=abc123 status=429 message=rate limit exceeded retry_after=60
2026-03-18T14:22:08Z ERROR scim-provisioner request_id=abc124 action=PATCH user=U-xxxx error="KMS decrypt failed: invalid ciphertext"
2026-03-18T14:22:09Z INFO audit role_change user=U-xxxx old_roles=[viewer] new_roles=[] reason=provisioning-error
```

maria: Looks like two concurrent issues: (1) Okta flooding our SCIM endpoint -> 429s, (2) KMS decrypt errors causing partial provisioning rollbacks -> users losing roles. We should correlate.

sanjay: For 429: check our SCIM rate limit config and the per-org burst policy. Also check if Okta retry/backoff hammered us. Can we get the IdP-side retry logs?

alex: I've asked the customer's Okta admin for their system logs. Meanwhile, I checked our SCIM metrics: 14:20-14:30 we had a spike to 120 req/s, our per-org soft limit is 75/s. Throttling triggered auto-429.

chris: On KMS side: those decrypt errors mean the ciphertext shape didn't match key version. Possible causes: staged key rotation, or the payload was re-encrypted by a different key id. Ask infra if a key rotation job ran at 14:21.

irene: I'm pulling KMS audit trail now. Also can we check whether we persisted any partially-applied role changes? Our repro logic should be transactional but if decrypt failed mid-transaction we might have left role state inconsistent.

okta-bot: Notice: customer okta org "acme-inc" sent 3 bulk group pushes during 2026-03-18T14:20:00Z - 14:25:00Z (groups: eng, infra, contractors).

maria: If Okta retried quickly (no exponential backoff) we can overwhelm the per-org quota. We should: (A) temporarily raise per-org soft limit to let the backlog clear, (B) enable more aggressive client-side 429 backoff guidance in our SCIM response, (C) put a short circuit on role mutation until KMS errors resolved. Thoughts?

sanjay: +1. For (A) we can bump to 150/s for 10 minutes. Ops must approve. For (C) we need a migration-safe toggle: prevent applying role removals during a provisioning run if KMS fails for any role blob. Fallback to enqueue for retry.

chris: I already opened a FIXME in the provisioner: currently we apply per-attribute atomically but don't checkpoint on KMS decrypt failures. I'll attach a small patch to switch to apply-on-success only. Quick snippet: 

```
# pseudo
with transaction():
  for role_blob in role_updates:
    plaintext = kms.decrypt(role_blob.ciphertext)
    if not plaintext:
      raise DecryptError
    apply_role_change(user, plaintext)
```

maria: Good. Ops: can you check KMS key activity? If a rotation job started, rollback or ensure decryption compatibility. Also check if KMS returned a transient 5xx vs permanently invalid ciphertext.

irene: KMS audit shows a key rotation job started at 14:20:58 but completed at 14:21:10 — there are a handful of decryption requests using the old key id that returned INVALID_CIPHERTEXT between 14:21:02 and 14:21:12. This matches the error window.

alex: So root cause: Okta bulk/group pushes -> spikes -> 429s; concurrently a KMS key rotation produced invalid decrypts for a short window -> provisioner applied partial changes and removed roles. We need both mitigation and a follow-up to avoid recurrence.

maria: Immediate mitigations: 
- Temporarily raise SCIM per-org soft limit for acme-inc to 150/s for 15m (ops).
- Pause scheduled key rotations for 5m and audit rotation procedure (infra).
- Rehydrate affected users' roles from SSO group membership snapshot (we keep snapshots in S3) rather than manual edits.

sanjay: I'll run a rehydration job that reads the last-good SCIM snapshot at 14:19 and reapplies role mappings with idempotent checks. Estimated 8 minutes.

chris: I'll push the provisioner patch to avoid apply-on-partial-decrypt and add a metric for decrypt-failures that increments a counter per-user to alert earlier.

irene: I've saved the KMS audit slice and will open an infra incident to review rotation tooling. Also raising an alert rule: >=3 INVALID_CIPHERTEXT in 60s -> page oncall.

alex: Customer notified: we told them we saw Okta bulk pushes and a transient KMS rotation collision; we initiated a rehydration and will confirm when done. Waiting on ops to bump limit.

ops (sidenote): bump approved for 15m (done at 2145679400).

alex: Rehydration kicked off at 2145679600. I'll update when finished.

maria: Postmortem action items (assign after ops/infra return findings): 
- Harden SCIM to gracefully queue when KMS decrypts fail.
- Add per-org adaptive rate-limiting + SLO for bulk pushes.
- Improve rotation procedure: ensure crypto forwards compatibility during short windows.
- Add audit playbook that maps KMS decrypt errors -> potential provisioning impact.

alex: Rehydration done at 2145682100. Roles restored for 98% of affected users, 2% needed manual fix due to stale externalIds. I've DM'd the customer with a summary.

chris: Closing checklist: deploy provisioner patch to staging (in progress), infra to produce post-rotation compatibility test, add alert rule.

maria: Thanks everyone. Filing this thread as incident-zoom:scim-kms-rot for follow-up notes.

alex: tagging @sanjay @chris @irene for postmortem. :thumbsup:
